**Subject: 25-hour CVR / 140+ hour FDR recorders — competitor activity, Jan 2021 – Sep 2026 evidence window. Tier 2 public sources only (no user data supplied).**

## Key Insights

- **FACT — High confidence:** Airbus selected Acron Aviation's SRVIVR25 as its 25-hour CVR solution in October 2025, described in the joint release as "the only 25-hour CVR approved and qualified by Airbus thus far," distributed via Airbus service bulletin.
- **FACT — High confidence:** Honeywell's HCR-25 is built on Curtiss-Wright Fortress technology under a 2019 partnership in which Curtiss-Wright is "the exclusive supplier of Honeywell's next-generation recorders" — two of the eight named competitors share one design authority.
- **OBSERVATION — Medium/High confidence:** Two of the eight named competitors (Thales, RUAG) show no public evidence of a current crash-protected recorder product; RUAG's own March 2026 disclosure states it has exited non-space businesses entirely.
- **FACT — High confidence:** Both of the two largest Western recorder franchises changed corporate form inside 15 months — L3Harris CAS sold to TJC (31 Mar 2025, ~$800M) becoming Acron, and Honeywell Aerospace spun off as HONA (29 Jun 2026).
- **FACT — Medium confidence:** Curtiss-Wright publishes 210+ hours @ 4,096 wps for the Fortress FDR-25 — the highest FDR duration found publicly, well above the 140-hour benchmark that defines the subject product.

*Legend: GROWTH = documented commercial expansion · STABLE = active product, no new event · EMERGING = announced, not yet in service · GRAY = insufficient current data · DECLINING = documented exit.*

**INTERPRETATION (Medium):** The eight-competitor framing overstates the number of independent competitors; the evidence supports roughly four independent recorder design authorities in the 25-hour class (Acron, Curtiss-Wright, Universal/Elbit, Safran), plus one announced entrant. *So what: the competitive set for a 25h/140h product is narrower and more concentrated than vendor-list market reports imply, and a Honeywell win and a Curtiss-Wright win are not independent events.*

## Competitor profiles

**Acron Aviation (ex-L3Harris Commercial Aviation Solutions).** St. Petersburg, FL; CEO Alan Crawford; ~$800M revenue, 1,400 employees, PE-owned by TJC since 31 Mar 2025; facilities in the UK, US, Thailand and India (Source: FlightGlobal / Aviation Today, Mar–Apr 2025). L3Harris disclosed the divestiture would reduce expected 2025 revenue by ~$525M (Source: Reuters via iTiger, 24 Apr 2025) — **FACT, High**. *So what: the recorder franchise now sits in a standalone entity whose growth depends on this portfolio rather than on a diversified defence parent.* Product positioning is explicitly retrofit-friendly: 9.79 lb, ARINC 757 form-fit direct replacement for FA2100 with "no aircraft rewiring or mounting changes," 90-day non-hazmat ULB, ED-112A with stated evolution to ED-112B, standardised part numbers across line-fit and retrofit (Sources: acronaviation.com; Military & Aerospace Electronics, 17 Oct 2025) — **FACT (vendor), Medium**. Note an unresolved internal inconsistency: Acron marketing elsewhere claims "50+ hours of voice recording and 140+ hours of flight data at 2,048 wps," against the 25h/140h framing in the same catalogue — **UNKNOWN, Low**. *So what: the headline 25h figure appears to be a compliance floor rather than a hardware ceiling, which weakens duration as a differentiator.*

**Curtiss-Wright.** Manufactures at Bournemouth, England; claims recorder heritage to 1957 and first certification of a 25-hour ICAO Class 6 CVR — a claim contested implicitly by Acron's "60+ years" marketing (**FACT (vendor), Medium**). Launch cadence is the densest in the set: Fortress FDR-25/CVR-25 (Sep 2022, DO-178C/DO-254 DAL D, form-and-fit for many applications) and Fortress CSR (Jan 2023, claimed industry-first CVFDR combining 25h recording with data acquisition, RIPS and QAR in one unit). Q3 2025 guidance names "increased sales of avionics and flight data recorders" as a Commercial Aerospace growth driver, with Defense Electronics guided to $1,000–1,010M, +10–11% (Source: CW Form 8-K Ex-99.2, 5 Nov 2025) — **FACT, High**. *So what: this is the only public filing in the evidence base that ties recorder demand directly to a named supplier's disclosed revenue trajectory.*

**Honeywell (HONA from 29 Jun 2026).** HCR-25 EASA TSO in Jan 2021; type-certified on Boeing 737/767/777 in Jun 2023; A320-family certification slated H1 2025 (**FORECAST as published**). Weight <9.5 lb / 4.3 kg — effectively at parity with the SRVIVR25's 9.79 lb (**FACT, High**). A separate lightweight family (LW-CVR, LW-FDR 25h, LW-HR25, KDR100, AeroCorder 100) coexists with HCR-25. Forward: CVDR 25 "expected to have… certified in 2027," described by Honeywell's Vlacic as "smaller and lighter than our HCR 25, so it's optimized for more business aircraft" (Source: NBAA Business Aviation Insider, Jul 2026) — **FORECAST, Medium**. *So what: the next competitive round is being contested on business-aviation SWaP rather than on recording duration.*

**Universal Avionics (an Elbit Systems company — not Safran; correction, High confidence, Source: UA releases 2020 & 15 May 2024).** KAPTURE launched 2 Sep 2020, 6th generation, FAA TSO / ED-112A, lithium-free 90-day ULB, patented internal RIPS, capacitor pack replacing batteries; FDR capacity 90h ARINC 717 plus 25h via ARINC 429 (**FACT, Medium — single source**). Certified across Gulfstream, Embraer, De Havilland Canada, HondaJet and Textron; typical 6–8 hour overnight installation; CEO Dror Yahav cites "a remarkable retrofit market opportunity" (Source: Aviation Week, 7 May 2025) — **FACT, High**. Added Flight Recorder Readout Services in May 2024 — **FACT, High**. *So what: Universal's disclosed FDR capacity of ~90–115h sits below the 140h subject benchmark, positioning it on installation speed and business-jet certification breadth rather than duration.*

**Safran.** Helicopter CVFDR records 25h of flight data and 2h of audio (Source: safran-group.com) — **FACT, High**. *So what: Safran's publicly documented rotorcraft product is not in the 25-hour-voice class, so it competes adjacently rather than head-to-head.* B.SAFE (ENERTEC brand) serves defence. Preligens AI acquisition (Sep 2024, $243.3M) is adjacent, tertiary-sourced — **Low**.

**Leonardo DRS.** ADFR deployable recorder designed and built by DRS Technologies Canada, integrated by L3 for Airbus (2017 agreement; Airbus A350-1000 testing 2021; 25h combined capacity; certification was "on schedule" for Q2 2020, EIS "on target" for 2021). No 2024–2026 recorder announcement surfaced — **UNKNOWN, Medium**. *So what: the lapsed schedule with no public update is a missed-milestone signal for civil deployable recorders, and Leonardo DRS's current civil channel appears to run through Acron's partnership rather than independently.*

**Thales — UNKNOWN.** No CVR/FDR appears in Thales's own public catalogue after two targeted searches; its verified tie to this market is the ACSS joint venture with Acron (**Medium**). **RUAG — UNKNOWN / likely legacy.** RUAG International states it "is now fully focused on the space business" (24 Mar 2026), directly contradicting a Feb 2026 analyst report naming RUAG as a CVFDR niche player (**High** that the contradiction exists). *So what: at least two names in circulating analyst vendor lists are unsupported by primary disclosure, so any share model built on those lists inherits stale structure.*

## Market observations

**OBSERVATION (High):** Every credible competitor markets form-fit-function replacement as its primary design constraint — Acron ARINC 757 drop-in, Curtiss-Wright "form-and-fit," Universal adapter tray, Honeywell lightweight variants. *So what: differentiation is migrating away from recording duration toward installation labour, channel access and spares commonality.*

**OBSERVATION (Medium):** Route to market is bifurcating between OEM service-bulletin channels (Acron–Airbus; Honeywell HCR-25 orderable "directly from Boeing or Honeywell") and open aftermarket retrofit. *So what: airframer qualification is becoming a gating asset independent of product specification.*

**OBSERVATION (Medium):** Non-traditional entrants are appearing at both ends — a tooling vendor (Flight Data Systems) moving into recorder hardware, and an MRO (Lufthansa Technik) marketing its own 25h-capable CVFDR. *So what: the "high barrier to entry" characterisation in analyst reports is being tested from adjacent positions in the value chain.*

**UNKNOWN:** No list price, price announcement, contract value, warranty term, or unit-share figure was found for any named vendor. The only monetary anchors are FAA analytical assumptions ($25,000 unit cost; ~$5,209 incremental 25h-vs-2h in 2024 dollars), which are regulatory inputs, not market prices. No carbon, recycled-content or lifecycle sustainability claims were found — only hazmat/logistics claims around ULB batteries.

## Confidence Summary

The structural spine of this report rests on High-confidence evidence: the Acron–Airbus selection, the Curtiss-Wright–Honeywell exclusive supply relationship, both corporate separations, all Honeywell certification milestones, the Universal/Elbit ownership correction, and RUAG's exit are each sourced to company releases, SEC filings, wire services or OEM announcements. Product specification and positioning claims — weights, capacities, installation times, ED-112B readiness — are predominantly Medium confidence because they are vendor-published and rarely independently verified; the SRVIVR25's 140-hour figure is the exception, corroborated by a third-party distributor listing. Forward statements (Honeywell CVDR 25 in 2027, Flight Data Systems Sentry 25h) are Medium-confidence forecasts carrying company-stated timing only. The principal gaps are: no pricing or warranty data for any vendor; no unit-volume or market-share data; unresolved status of Leonardo DRS's civil ADFR programme; an unexplained inconsistency in Acron's own voice-duration claims (25h vs 50+h); and a documented conflict between February 2026 analyst vendor lists and March 2026 company disclosure regarding RUAG. Thales and RUAG should be treated as unverified in this category pending Tier 1 data.
